title: Sub-lemma E: verify F has degrees independent of n and contains no A^(t) (the two structural constraints are part of the theorem)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Issue.** Two of the three required properties of $\mathbf F$ are structural and must be *verified*, not assumed: (1) the degrees of the coordinate functions are independent of $n$; (2) $\mathbf F$ does not depend on $A^{(1)},\dots,A^{(n)}$.

**What must be proved.** Each coordinate built in Sub-lemma A involves $O(1)$ cells and a contraction $\Phi$ of bounded degree; hence the degree is independent of $n$ even though the number of coordinates $N$ grows with $n$. A-independence: $\Phi$ is a fixed contraction template applied to the *given* masked tensors, with no $A^{(t)}$ appearing in the coefficients. A finite-generation/Noetherianity argument is needed to argue the bounded-degree family of relations suffices for all $n$.

**Note.** This is exactly where an otherwise-correct construction can fail the problem's literal requirements.
